## Description

`\PA\` through `\PI\` selects ISO-8859-1 through ISO-8859-9 (one upper-case letter, persistent for the rest of the string). Real files emit lowercase letters (`\Pg\`), digits (`\P1\`), full names (`\PISO\`), or omit/replace the selector (`\P\`, `\P!\`). Many parsers also skip the state machine and ignore the directive entirely, garbling subsequent characters.

## Reproducer recipe

`'\PB\Krak\X\F3w'` (Polish "Kraków" via Latin-2); `'\Pg\\S\a'` (lowercase selector); `'\P1\…'` (digit); `'\P!\X\41'` (non-letter).

## Expected kernel behavior

validate `[A-I]` per Table 4; emit `E_BAD_PAGE_DIRECTIVE` for out-of-range; implement the page-state machine at minimum for `\PA\`; warn that decoding may be incorrect when the state is not implemented.
